speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the vaccination take-up rate for adults for conditions like pneumococcal disease and influenza after the launch of the National Adult Immunisation Schedule in 2017; and (b) how do our rates of adult vaccination compare with other developed countries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These vaccinations include catch-up vaccinations and vaccinations that high-risk adults should receive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: To encourage more Singaporeans to get vaccinated, MediSave may be used to pay for NAIS vaccinations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: While this increasing vaccination take-up rate is encouraging, we note that the take-up of adult vaccination is higher in countries where there are more established adult vaccination programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We can do more to promote adult vaccinations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Details of these subsidies will be announced at a later date.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MOH is also planning a series of population-level vaccination awareness campaigns to increase awareness on the importance of vaccination.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just one supplementary question, which is that, in determining the quantum of subsidies, does the Ministry actually do modelling whereby you look at the cost of MediFund, hospital subsidies and so on and so forth that will be saved if the vaccine take-up is increased, and you sort of use that as a way to calculate how large the subsidy should be, such that it is fiscally neutral or it may even be fiscally positive?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Because it would seem to me that there would be savings as the vaccination take-up increases and that should be used as a basis to make these vaccines either highly subsidised or possibly even free in many cases.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We are in the midst of crafting the package and we will announce it when we have the details.
